statement: A linear function $f$ satisfies $f(2) = 7$ and $f\big(f(2)\big) = 22$. What is the value of $f(0)$?

choices.misconception: I read $f(f(2))$ as $f(2 \cdot 2) = f(4)$, so I used a slope of $\frac{22 - 7}{4 - 2} = 7.5$ and got $7 - 15 = -8$.
I found the slope, $3$, and gave that as the answer instead of the value of $f$ at $x = 0$.
I found the slope of $3$ but moved the wrong way: going from $x = 2$ down to $x = 0$, I added $2 \cdot 3$ to $7$ instead of subtracting.

hints: You now know two points on the line: $(2, 7)$ and $(7, 22)$. Find the slope, then step back from $x = 2$ to $x = 0$.

solutions.reliable: Because $f(2) = 7$, we have $f(f(2)) = f(7) = 22$. The line passes through $(2, 7)$ and $(7, 22)$, so its slope is $\frac{22 - 7}{7 - 2} = \frac{15}{5} = 3$. Then $f(x) = 7 + 3(x - 2) = 3x + 1$, and $f(0) = 1$. Check: $f(7) = 22$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
